items_missed: No agenda statement at all — went straight from "what was your preferred date" into data collection. Never laid out the roadmap, never gave the 10-15 minute timeframe, never asked for confirmation.
Never asked "How are you today?" — customer opened with "Hi, good morning" and Calvin answered with "Yeah, what was your preferred date next week?"

Never asked about packing needs. Customer is moving from a storage unit with "couch mattress rugs" and boxes — packing services and materials were never raised, and packing-service pricing was never quoted.
Said "So boxes and then the destination address" but never asked how many boxes — box count went entirely uncaptured on a 10x10 storage move.
Never asked the moving-stressor question — no version of "is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?"
Destination zip code never captured. Got "403 west else place, apartment three" and a floor, but no zip — origin got a full zip (78258), destination did not.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned — no reference to the pre-move email with the mover's photo and info.

No Worries Damage Coverage named but not explained. Said "It's high evaluation for your items just to give you peace of mind" with no $2,000 per-move figure, no repair/replace/reimburse language, and no 60 cents-per-pound industry baseline to contrast against.
"No hidden fees" pitch was partial — covered no trip fees, no taxes, no credit card fees, but omitted no fuel surcharge and no assembly fees.
No sense-check after the clock explanation. Delivered rate, 2.5-hour minimum, $480, and 15-minute increments in one unbroken block and never asked "does that make sense?"
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing — no prep-equals-shorter-move-equals-lower-bill framing, no consolidation examples, no "take a carload" tip, no close.
Stairs identified but never priced into the estimate. Confirmed the destination is a second-floor walk-up and then never told her stairs add time to the clock.
Drive time between the storage unit and the apartment never explained as billable clock time on a two-location move.
Walk distance discussed only at origin ("third from the door") — never at the destination.
Never used the customer's name. Had "Sydney" spelled out for him and used it zero times in the call.
Email handoff mentioned but not explained — no bolded-details-at-the-top framing, no "reply with any corrections" verification ask.
Never gave hours or how to reach the office.
top_strength: Ruthless efficiency with a real rapport moment inside it. Calvin booked a move in five and a half minutes without the call ever feeling rushed to the customer, who closed with "perfect, cool, well that sounds great. Thank you so much." He led with the scorecard opener verbatim — "our pricing super simple so yeah, I can run through that real quick" — then delivered rate, inclusions, minimum, increments, and a dollar range in one clean pass, and asked for the booking directly: "there's no deposit or anything required to book where you want to get anything scheduled." The best moment was unscripted: he noticed she was a repeat customer ("It looks like we also moved your way back in 2021 as well"), which got a warm reaction and instant trust. He also volunteered the day-before courtesy text, which is good expectation-setting nobody asked him for.
coaching_note: Calvin, the highest-leverage fix is the Save Your Ass prep speech — it is worth 10 points and you left all 10 on the table on a move where it directly applies. She is going from a 10x10 unit into a second-floor walk-up: that is the exact job where prep changes the bill. Say it like this: "One thing that saves you real money — anything you can consolidate or carry yourself before we get there makes the move shorter, and since you're paying by the time, shorter move means a smaller bill. Loose items in drawers, rugs rolled and banded, anything small enough to take a carload — get that done and you'll likely land at the low end of that range. Does that make sense?" That single block also gives you your missing sense-check. Second priority: your No Worries explanation was too vague to be useful. "It's high evaluation for your items" tells her nothing — she needs "up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace, or reimburse accidental damages, versus the 60-cents-per-pound the industry standard gives you." Third, add the agenda opener; it costs you fifteen seconds and you have never once earned that point. And use her name — you had Sydney spelled out letter by letter and used it zero times. BUSINESS RISKS: (1) You confirmed her destination is a second-floor unit and then quoted "the minimum to maybe 3.5 hours" without ever telling her stairs add time — same for the drive between the storage unit and the apartment, which is billable clock she does not know about. That $480-$672 range is the number she is expecting, and a stairs-plus-drive overage is exactly how estimate accuracy gets missed and a customer feels blindsided. Set the ceiling honestly on the call. (2) The destination zip was never captured — verify the address before the confirmation email goes out or the crew routes wrong. (3) Confirm the verbal $480-$672 range and the 8:30-9:00 AM window actually made it into EMMA, since the booking was closed entirely by voice.
phone_presence_notes: Pleasant and upbeat with repeated "Awesome!" affirmations and one genuine rapport moment on the 2021 repeat-customer catch, but otherwise transactional — zero use of her name, no empathy markers, and several clipped transitions that jumped straight to the next data field ("So boxes and then the destination address").
